name: Loratadine
summary: Non-sedating second-generation antihistamine for allergic rhinitis and urticaria, dosed once daily.
mechanism: Peripheral H1 receptor antagonist; limited CNS penetration underlies its non-sedating profile.

dosing.renalAdjustment: CrCl < 30 mL/min or significant hepatic impairment: 10 mg every other day

safety.pregnancy: Extensive clinical experience; no major teratogenicity demonstrated
safety.lactation: Excreted in breast milk; generally considered compatible
warnings: Occasional somnolence — advise caution when driving initially
Reduce dose in hepatic impairment and CrCl < 30 mL/min
Check OTC cold products for other antihistamines (duplication)
monitoring: Response; hepatic/renal function for dose adjustment
safety.overdose: Generally benign (headache, sedation, tachycardia) — supportive care

clinicalPearls: Less sedating than cetirizine for many patients — a reasonable switch when sedation is an issue
Onset takes 1–3 h; it is not for acute allergic reactions or anaphylaxis
good: Once-daily, effectively non-sedating control of allergic rhinitis and hives
bad: Acute anaphylaxis or rapid-onset urticaria; hepatic/renal impairment without dose adjustment
